```{r load-pkg, message = FALSE, eval = FALSE}

library(tidyverse)

```

## Background and target

Researchers tested whether sleep restriction affects memory for emotional and neutral words. Participants were assigned to either a well-rested condition with eight hours of sleep or a sleep-restricted condition with four hours of sleep. The next morning, participants completed a recall task containing 20 neutral words and 20 emotional words.

![](sleep_memory_goal.png)

## Import and inspect the data

```{r import-data, eval = FALSE}

memory_raw <- read_csv(
  "sleep_memory_messy.csv",
  na = c("", "NA", "missing", "999")
)

glimpse(memory_raw)
nrow(memory_raw)

memory_raw %>% count(sleep_group)
memory_raw %>% count(test_order)
memory_raw %>% count(attention_check)

```

## Clean, reshape, and recode the data

```{r clean-data, eval = FALSE}

memory_clean <- memory_raw %>%
  distinct() %>%
  mutate(
    participant_id = str_to_upper(participant_id),
    age_years = parse_number(age),

    sleep_group = str_to_lower(sleep_group),
    sleep_group = str_replace_all(sleep_group, " ", "_"),
    sleep_condition = case_when(
      sleep_group %in% c(
        "8_hours",
        "rested",
        "full_sleep"
      ) ~ "Well-rested",
      sleep_group %in% c(
        "4_hours",
        "restricted",
        "short_sleep"
      ) ~ "Sleep-restricted",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    test_order = str_to_lower(test_order),
    test_order = case_when(
      test_order %in% c(
        "neutral first",
        "neutral_first",
        "nf"
      ) ~ "Neutral first",
      test_order %in% c(
        "emotional first",
        "emotional_first",
        "ef"
      ) ~ "Emotional first",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    attention_check = str_to_lower(attention_check),
    passed_attention = attention_check %in% c("pass", "passed", "y")
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(neutral_recall, emotional_recall),
    names_to = "word_type",
    values_to = "recall_raw"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    word_type = case_when(
      word_type == "neutral_recall" ~ "Neutral words",
      word_type == "emotional_recall" ~ "Emotional words",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    recall_score = parse_number(recall_raw),
    sleep_condition = factor(
      sleep_condition,
      levels = c("Well-rested", "Sleep-restricted")
    ),
    word_type = factor(
      word_type,
      levels = c("Neutral words", "Emotional words")
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(
    passed_attention == TRUE,
    !is.na(sleep_condition),
    !is.na(word_type),
    !is.na(recall_score),
    between(recall_score, 0, 20)
  ) %>%
  select(
    participant_id,
    age_years,
    sleep_condition,
    test_order,
    word_type,
    recall_score
  )

```

## Check the cleaned data

```{r check-cleaning, eval = FALSE}

nrow(memory_clean) # 83

memory_clean %>%
  count(sleep_condition, word_type)

memory_clean %>%
  group_by(sleep_condition, word_type) %>%
  summarize(
    median_recall = median(recall_score),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

```

Expected counts and medians:

| Sleep condition | Word type | N | Median |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Well-rested | Neutral words | 21 | 14 |
| Well-rested | Emotional words | 21 | 16 |
| Sleep-restricted | Neutral words | 20 | 10 |
| Sleep-restricted | Emotional words | 21 | 12 |

## Create the target boxplot

```{r target-boxplot, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 6, eval = FALSE}

ggplot(
  memory_clean,
  aes(
    x = sleep_condition,
    y = recall_score,
    fill = word_type
  )
) +
  geom_boxplot(
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.80),
    width = 0.65,
    alpha = 0.78
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    limits = c("Well-rested", "Sleep-restricted")
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = c(5, 10, 15, 20)
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(4, 20)) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Neutral words" = "#56B4E9",
      "Emotional words" = "#CC79A7"
    ),
    breaks = c("Neutral words", "Emotional words")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Word recall by sleep condition",
    x = "Sleep condition",
    y = "Words recalled (out of 20)",
    fill = "Word type"
  ) +
  theme_classic()

```
